en.headline: Police use drones to record 42 double-white-line offences in Southern District
en.dek: Officers from the Hong Kong Island Traffic Unit targeted Stanley Gap Road and Victoria Road during Operation Torch today.
body: Hong Kong police used drones for high-altitude recording during a traffic enforcement operation in the Southern District today. The Hong Kong Island Traffic Unit said the exercise, codenamed Torch, targeted illegal racing and double-white-line crossings.

Acting Chief Inspector Wong Ka-wing of the unit’s Operations and Control Group said officers recorded 42 instances of vehicles crossing double white lines on Stanley Gap Road and Victoria Road. The roads are narrow and winding, and irresponsible driving can endanger other road users.

Police said drones allowed evidence to be gathered with less disruption to traffic. Drivers who commit dangerous driving face a maximum fine of HK$25,000 and three years’ imprisonment, plus a minimum six-month driving ban under the Road Traffic Ordinance.
The force said it would continue intelligence-led operations using technology to combat unsafe driving.

zh.headline: 警方南區以無人機執法 錄得42宗橫越雙白線
zh.dek: 港島總區交通部今日展開「火炬」行動，於赤柱峽道及域多利道以高空錄影搜集證據。
body: 香港警方今日在南區展開交通執法行動，使用無人機進行高空錄影。港島總區交通部表示，代號「火炬」的行動針對非法賽車及橫越雙白線等違例駕駛行為。
該部執行及管制組署理總督察黃嘉穎表示，行動期間在赤柱峽道及域多利道一帶錄得42宗車輚橫越雙白線。該等路段路窄彎多，不負責任的駕駛行為可能危及其他道路使用者。
警方指，無人機可在較少干擾其他道路使用者的情況下搜集證據。根據《道路交通條例》，危險駕駛最高可被判罰款二萬五千元及監禁三年，並停牌至少六個月。
警方表示會繼續以情報主導，配合科技不定時展開行動，打擊危害道路安全的駕駛行為。
